tools.description: List the HOST-BOUND indicators a Rhai strategy can actually call — what the vike-rhai host registers, which is not every vike-indicators registry name; a script calling an unbound one compiles and then fails on every bar. Your own (user_data/indicators) come under `user_indicators`. No arguments returns the compact roster (name + category). Pass `category` for one family in full, or `name` for one indicator in full — its parameters with defaults and its output line — which also answers WHY a registry name is not callable. The roster is not repeated in this text on purpose: it is long, and a description is sent whether you call the tool or not.

category.description: one family, in full — the `category` value the roster reports (case-insensitive)

name.description: one indicator, in full (its parameters with defaults, and the value it returns) — or, for a registry name the host holds back, the reason

tools.description: What a backtest profile TOML may say, read from the published profile schema this build's backtest daemon parses (the release's profile.json). With no argument: every table, "" the top level, with its key names. With `table`: each of its keys in full — type, required, default, the words it takes and what it means. Write run_backtest's, run_sweep's and run_walk_forward's `profile` from it. Offline — no server.

table.description: one table in full, by the name the table list gives (engine, data.series, "" for the top level): each key's type, whether it is required, its default, the words it takes and what it means. Omitted: every table with its key names

tools.name: profile_template
tools.title: Show backtest settings

tools.description: Say what an order client id means: who placed it (G GUI, C CLI, T Telegram, M this server, S a strategy, E the engine), the strategy and account codes, whether it opens or closes and which way, its group and role (entry, stop, take-profit) and its replacement number, as JSON with one plain-words line (`words`). Works with no node; with --node and this box's device key on the node's access list (role observe or higher), outside --profile offline, it adds the names the node gives: the account's label, the strategy behind the code, and the group's other orders resting now. `node` says where the names came from: read, unreachable (`node_error` says why, and the names are null), none (no --node) or offline (this profile reads no node). `form` is v2, v1 (an id minted before these codes) or other (a venue's own id, a foreign order's, one typed by hand). Labels decide nothing. Read-only.

order_client_id.description: the id to read, as an order, a fill or a preview shows it
